The manipulation of time in the story is very effective and well-balanced. The actual "story time" consists of just a few minutes as the protagonist enters the house and walks from the hallway to the pantry. The writer stretches these brief moments through rich sensory details (the creaking hinge, the smell of cold dust, the worn linoleum, the darkened quince jelly), which creates a quiet, suspenseful atmosphere and emphasizes the weight of her return. At the same time, the writer skillfully compresses twenty years of absence into a few brief observations—such as her momentary failure to recognize her own aging reflection and the faded date on the jar. This balance between the stretched-out present and the compressed past makes the final revelation in the last sentence hit with just the right amount of dramatic impact.
